title: Braking time
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the braking time as 4 s, using the average velocity or appropriate kinematics.

title: Resistance force magnitude
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the resistance force as 2.5 × 10³ N, applying Newton's second law after finding acceleration.

title: Children crossing time
description: Important: The response must correctly calculate the total time for the children to cross as 24 s, using the total distance (l+L) and their walking speed.

title: Required waiting time
description: Essential: The response must correctly determine the waiting time before the crosswalk as 20 s, subtracting the braking time from the children's crossing time.

title: Final speed for higher initial speed
description: Essential: The response must correctly calculate the car's speed when reaching the crossing for part (4) as 5√5 m/s, using kinematics with the previously found acceleration.

title: Use of constant acceleration kinematics
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply kinematics for constant acceleration (e.g., v² = u² + 2as) to relate distance, initial speed, and acceleration.

title: Unit conversion error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student fails to convert velocity from km/h to m/s before performing calculations.

title: Sign error in acceleration
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly assigns a positive sign to the deceleration in force or kinematic equations, leading to a nonsensical result.

title: Alternative solution check
description: Optional: Award credit if the student verifies an answer using a different valid method or performs a unit analysis on the final force.
